newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WALES AND TURKEY IN 0-0 WORLD CUP STALEMATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WALES AND TURKEY IN 0-0 WORLD CUP STALEMATE.

text.p: Wales and Turkey slipped further out of the reckoning for World Cup places on Saturday when they drew 0-0 in a drab qualifier in Cardiff.
The result means the Netherlands and Belgium, who were meeting in Brussels later in the day, are clear favourites to qualify from European group seven.

The Turks came closest to breaking the deadlock when Kemalettin Senturk rattled the crossbar with a second half strike and then forced a fine save from goalkeeper Neville Southall with an overhead kick.
Wales, beaten 7-1 by the Dutch in their last World Cup outing, came to life in the final minutes when Chelsea striker Mark Hughes twice came close to scoring the winner.
Wales' single point takes them top of the group on seven points, one ahead of both the Dutch and the Belgians, who both have three games in hand on Bobby Gould's side.
Wales - Neville Southall, Stephen Jenkins, Robbie Page, Vinnie Jones, Andy Melville, Mark Pembridge, Barry Horne, Dean Saunders (Charlie Hartson 81), Gary Speed, Mark Hughes, Ryan Giggs.

Turkey - Engin Ipekoglu, Recep Cetin, Erol Bulent, Kemalettin Senturk (Tolunay Kafkas 88), Alpay Ozalan, Abdullah Ercan, Ilker Yagcioglu, Ogun Temizkanoglu, Hakan Sukur, Tugay Kerimolgu, Arif Erdem (Okray 70)
